messages:
Alex G: Hey support — customer on private VPC gateway started getting 429s and auth failures after they tightened the rate limiter. They also reported billing spikes (unexpected token counts) when clients retried. Timeline: config change at 2026-03-12T15:02Z. Root cause suspected: quota exhaustion + aggressive retry/backoff causing token churn. Attaching sample envoy config they applied.

Kevin Patel: Thanks Alex — can you paste the gateway rate-limiter config and any ingress k8s annotations? also need the first/last request ids and edge logs.

Alex G: pasted config snippet:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  envoy_rate_limit: |
    domain: customer-gw
    descriptors:
      - key: remote_addr
        value: "{{ remote_addr }}"
    token_bucket:
      fill_interval: 100ms
      fill_rate: 100
      max_tokens: 200
```
They also have k8s ingress annotations:
`kubectl describe ingress customer-gw` output: `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "10"`

Maria Chen: That token_bucket looks like a per-IP global bucket at fill_rate 100/s and burst 200 — with many ephemeral clients that can quickly deplete the global quota. Also nginx limit-connections doesn't smooth per-second bursts. Suggest switch to leaky-bucket or increase fill_rate and set a longer refill interval. Also disable aggressive client retry for 429.

Jordan (SRE): Repro steps we need: 1) reproduce with a small load generator that mimics retry-after behavior (10% clients backoff 100-500ms) 2) collect envoy ratelimit check logs with `--log-format` debug 3) get billing token counter per-route for the window. I'll drop a quick load command.

Jordan (SRE): Load repro (k6):
```bash
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 120s script.js
# script.js should simulate 10% clients retrying immediately on 429 with jitter
```

Kevin Patel: For immediate mitigation: temporarily raise max_tokens to 1000 and fill_rate to 500, or enable `burst_smoothing: true` on the gateway if supported. Also add response header `Retry-After` to guide clients. We can push a canary to 10% of traffic.

SRE-Bot: deploy-canary job started -> canary id c-20260312-01

Alex G: Can you confirm any billing implications? customer worried about token counts while we debug.

Support Bot: Short term: increasing burst will increase allowed tokens; that may increase billed units. Recommend documenting changes and notifying customer. Long term: implement per-api-key token buckets + per-ip fallback to avoid global exhaustion.

Maria Chen: Also check auth service 401 -> some clients refreshed tokens aggressively on 401 causing a wave of traffic. Add server-side token refresh throttling and backoff. We'll collect traces for auth calls.

Kevin Patel: I'll coordinate with customer to schedule a 30m window to apply canary and monitor p99 latency and 429 rates. Need sample request ids and customer approval.

Alex G: Customer approved canary window 16:30-17:00 UTC. I'll attach logs after run.

SRE-Bot: canary finished -> status: success; 429 dropped from 6% -> 0.5% for canary traffic; latency p99 unchanged.

Jordan (SRE): Post-mortem notes: root cause = global token bucket + client retry spikes + auth refresh churn. Action items: (1) ship per-api-key buckets (2) add default Retry-After headers (3) update docs for on-prem gateway tuning (4) billing alert if token rate jumps >2x baseline.

Alex G: Thanks all — filing follow-up ticket with config diffs and customer summary.
